tier_reason: Independent measurement: the page is succinctly's own comparison (author John Ky, rust-works/succinctly; maxi-tools/succinctly is a fork carrying a byte-identical copy), unrelated to the sucds author, and succinctly loses to sucds on select1, so there is no bias toward sucds. Harness is public (bench-compare/benches/succinct_libs.rs, features pinned in bench-compare/Cargo.toml, answers cross-checked by verify_agreement) and rustc 1.97.0 plus Apple M5 Max are stated, but optimisation flags are not stated (no [profile.bench] override or .cargo/config in the repo, so cargo bench defaults, no target-cpu), which keeps it short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: select1 (10,000 random queries, ARM64): sucds Rank9Sel 70.8-139.7 us vs vers-vecs RsVec 174.4-575.6 us, i.e. 1.3x (10M/10%) to 7.8x (1M/90%) faster (derived from page data), and vs succinctly BitVec 181.0-279.8 us, 1.6-3.4x faster (page states 1.6-3.4x). rank1: sucds 16.0-17.9 us, about level with succinctly (14.2-17.9 us; sucds slightly slower at 1M) and 1.8-2.1x faster than vers-vecs 30.0-34.0 us (derived from page data). sux-rs beats sucds on both rank1 and select1 in the same tables.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.97.0, cargo bench with criterion 0.5; sucds 0.8.3 with `intrinsics` feature (pinned in bench-compare/Cargo.toml); no [profile.bench] override, RUSTFLAGS or target-cpu stated, so default bench profile
corrections.caveats: Measured by the rival succinctly project (independent of sucds) on ARM64 only; x86_64 run outstanding. vers-vecs' SIMD select is AVX-512-only, so it ran scalar on ARM64 and its select could improve substantially on x86_64. sux-rs is faster than sucds in the same tables. select1 cells varied up to about 40% run to run; the page says read ordering, not ratios. Optimisation flags not stated. Baseline is other Rust crates, not SDSL or a C++ incumbent; vers-vecs is not a widely used incumbent. sucds construction is about 30-37x slower than vers-vecs because it has no bulk-word constructor (bit-at-a-time fill), and its resident overhead is 36% at 1M and 99% at 10M bits vs 5-7% for vers-vecs. Page benchmarked sucds 0.8.3; current release is 0.9.1. README has no performance numbers.

notes: All numbers match the page; the record's '6.6x at 1M/90%' was understated (page data gives 554.1/70.8 = 7.8x) and the succinctly select1 range starts at 181.0 not 195.9; corrected. Metadata checked: 108 stars, Apache-2.0 OR MIT, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-08-31.
